stranger: [m]Morning. Wipe your boots, the lane's wet.
[d]Afternoon. Passing through, or staying?
[e]Evening. Mind the cattle coming home.
[n]Late to be out. The Watch will have seen you.
Hunter, is it? No gate here, if that's your errand.
New face. We'll know your business by supper.
Keep to the path. Those fields are somebody's winter.
known: [m]Morning to you, {name}.
[d]Afternoon, {name}. Kept dry?
[e]Evening, {name}. The lamps are nearly lit.
[n]Out late, {name}. The Watch knows your step by now.
{name}. Good. You can stop looking lost.
There's {name} again. Mind the mud, it holds a grudge.
friend: {name}! Good to see you, and I mean it.
[m]Morning, {name}. You look almost rested.
[e]Evening, {name}. Come by the fire, the lane's no place to stand.
There you are. We'd started saving you a seat.
{name}, you're thinner. Eat something before you go.
[n]Still up, {name}? Come in out of the dark, then.
kin: {name}. Home, then. Properly home.
[m]Morning, {name}. Did you eat? Don't lie.
[e]There's our {name}. Supper stretches for one more.
Welcome back to {village}, {name}. It's your place as much as ours.
{name}! Somebody tell the dog.
[n]Come in, {name}. No door in {village} is bolted against you.

stranger: Mind the furrows. That's next year's bread.
[m]Up with the light, me. You too, it seems.
Use the verge, not the field. I'll know if you don't.
You've the look of a hunter. Is it gate trouble?
[d]Rain by supper. My knee has never been wrong.
known: [m]Morning, {name}. The barley's coming on.
{name}. Not on my seedlings, I hope.
[d]Afternoon, {name}. Hot work. There's water by the trough.
[e]Evening, {name}. One last row, then supper.
Good to see you, {name}. Harvest's close, so say it quick.
friend: {name}! Come to lean on my gate and watch me work? Welcome.
[m]Morning, {name}. Best wheat in years. Don't tell it I said so.
Take a turnip, {name}. Take two. They won't eat themselves.
You've saved us more than one good field, {name}. The soil remembers.
[e]Put your feet up on the wall, {name}. I'll finish the row.
kin: {name}. Soil under my nails, and glad to see you.
Whatever's in that basket is yours, {name}. It's your field too.
[m]Morning, {name}. I left your row. Don't look grateful, it's weeds.
Our own {name}. The crop knows you. I swear it leans.
[n]Stars out and you still up, {name}? Sit. I'll tell you the yield.

stranger: Hold still. You'll spook the flock.
[m]Dew's still on the grass. Mind your hem.
The dog doesn't like strangers. The dog is usually right.
Hunters bring trouble. Are you bringing trouble?
Keep your hand out of the fleece.
known: [m]Morning, {name}. The ewes are restless. Weather's turning.
{name}. The dog's decided you're all right. High praise.
[d]Afternoon, {name}. Quiet on the hill. I like it quiet.
[e]Evening, {name}. Counting heads. Stand still, you'll spoil it.
Good to see you, {name}. Count with me if you've nothing better.
friend: {name}! The lambs know your voice, I swear.
[m]Morning, {name}. Fancy the hill? I'll talk, you nod.
Sit, {name}. There's a flask and a warm rock, both yours.
The dog's been at the gate for you, {name}. It won't admit it.
[e]{name}, you walk like a hunter and sit like a shepherd now. Progress.
kin: {name}. You're one of the flock now. Don't wander off.
[m]Morning, {name}. The first lamb of spring was named for you. Sorry.
My dog, my hill and my flask, {name}. All yours.
You climbed the hill just to say hello, {name}? That's family.
[n]Out under the stars with me, {name}? Best shift there is.

stranger: Timber! ...Too late. You're fine.
Stand back from the fall line.
[m]Early for talk. Right time for firewood.
Hunter? Then you've a sharper axe than mine. Don't wave it.
Chips fly. Keep your eyes shut or your distance.
known: [m]Morning, {name}. Good oak down by the ridge.
{name}. Mind that log, it rolls.
[d]Afternoon, {name}. Sweat's honest work.
[e]Evening, {name}. Last cut, then I'm done.
Good to see you, {name}. Take a stack home if you've a hearth.
friend: {name}! Hold the axe a moment. See how it sits.
[m]Morning, {name}. I cut you a bundle of kindling. By the stump.
You stand like an oak these days, {name}. Steady. I mean it kindly.
The woods are quieter since you came, {name}. I won't ask why.
[e]{name}! Sit on the log. It's not wet. Mostly.
kin: {name}. The woodpile is yours. All of it. Don't look so shocked.
[m]Morning, {name}. I split a log for your fire and left it at your door.
Our {name}. I knew you'd come by. Kettle's on the stump.
The forest's your home too, {name}. I only keep the paths.
[n]Out this late, {name}? Take my lamp, the roots are tricky.

stranger: Coal on my hands. Don't shake, don't ask.
[m]Going down, coming up, tired either way.
Hunters dig too, I hear. Deeper than we do.
Lamp's lit, pick's sharp. Move along, friend.
Stay clear of the shaft mouth. It doesn't forgive.
known: [m]Morning, {name}. Early shift. Early dust.
{name}. The vein's thin today, but the ale's thick tonight.
[d]Afternoon, {name}. Come to see the daylight I've missed?
[e]Evening, {name}. Out of one dark, into the other. The inn.
Good to see you, {name}. Mind your head. Always.
friend: {name}! Show me your hands. Good. Working hands.
Down the shaft with me, {name}? A jest. Though you'd be handy.
[m]Morning, {name}. Found a seam of something shiny. Not telling where.
You've dirt on you, {name}. Suits you.
[e]Sit with the shift, {name}. We save the bench for friends.
kin: {name}. Down in the dark, you're the one I'd want behind me.
Take the best of what I've dug, {name}. It's a family share.
[m]Morning, {name}. The lamp's lit for you. Always is.
Come home with us, {name}. The dust washes off. The company doesn't.
[n]Night shift's easier with you about, {name}. Don't ask why.

stranger: Quiet. You'll frighten the fish.
[m]Dawn's the best bite. Don't talk.
Hunter? The river's got nothing for you but trout.
Mind the nets. They're my wages.
Keep your shadow off the water, if you can.
known: [m]Morning, {name}. Bite's good by the weir.
{name}. Caught a big one. It got away. That's the other kind of big.
[d]Afternoon, {name}. Slow day. Slow is fine.
[e]Evening, {name}. Last cast, then home.
Good to see you, {name}. You've a fisher's patience now.
friend: {name}! Take a rod. Doesn't matter if you catch. Matters that you sit.
[m]Morning, {name}. Smoked you a trout. It's by the nets.
You're good company at the water, {name}. Quiet. Rare.
The river likes you, {name}. It hasn't tipped you in yet.
[e]Sit by the bank fire, {name}. I'll gut, you talk.
kin: {name}. The best fish of the day was always yours. Don't ask where I hid it.
[m]Morning, {name}. The river's yours as much as mine. Stay and fish.
Our {name}. The boat's got your seat now. Not painted on. Yet.
{name}, you're home by the water. Sit. Talk. Or don't.
[n]Night lines are out, {name}. Help me pull, or keep me company.

stranger: Hunter to hunter: you're loud in the grass.
[d]I hunt deer. You hunt gates. Fair split.
Quiet. Something's moving in the brush.
[m]Frost holds a track best. You'd not know.
Keep your voice down. Game hears.
known: [m]Morning, {name}. Tracks along the stream. Fresh.
{name}. Meat's good this week. Come by the rack.
[d]Afternoon, {name}. Wind's wrong for a stalk. I'll rest.
[e]Evening, {name}. Heading home with a haunch.
Good to see you, {name}. You step quieter than you used to.
friend: {name}! Hunt the ridge with me at first light?
[m]Morning, {name}. I'll show you a track I've been saving.
You've the eye for it now, {name}. It's the gates that spoil you.
I'd walk the woods at night with you, {name}. Few I'd say that to.
[e]Sit, {name}. I'll tell you where the deer cross. Not a word to the others.
kin: {name}. The ridge is yours. Walk it whenever you like.
[m]Morning, {name}. I hung a haunch at your door. Eat it.
Our {name}. Best tracker in two valleys, and I'll say so to anyone.
I taught you half of it, {name}. You taught yourself the rest. Come eat.
[n]Night hunt, {name}? Come on, then. Quiet feet.

stranger: Make way! The wheel has no brake and I've no patience.
[m]Early start. It's a long road to Carillon.
Don't touch the load. It's counted.
Hunter? Ride the tail if you like. Pay in emeralds.
Road's rough. Cart's rougher.
known: [m]Morning, {name}. Loaded, ready, behind schedule.
{name}. Want the road news? It costs nothing.
[d]Afternoon, {name}. The axle squeals. It's trying to say something.
[e]Evening, {name}. Back from the city, and aching.
Good to see you, {name}. You walk faster than my horse.
friend: {name}! Hop on, I'll take you to the next village. No charge.
[m]Morning, {name}. Carillon says hello. Well, it shouts. It always shouts.
Brought you something from the city, {name}. Under the sacks.
Sit up front, {name}. The horse prefers you to me.
[e]The roads are better with you about, {name}. Odd, that.
kin: {name}. Any road, any hour. If I'm on it, you ride.
[m]Morning, {name}. Letters from the city, and a pie from my sister. Take both.
Our {name}! The horse knows your whistle.
You're why I'll drive after dark, {name}. Don't tell my wife.
[n]Night road, {name}? I'll light the lantern. Hop up.

stranger: I'm {elder}. This is {village}. State your business, kindly.
Hunter? We asked for none. We've never turned one away, though.
[m]Morning, traveller. The inn is warm and the bell is honest.
[e]Evening. Strangers are welcome until they aren't.
Welcome to {village}. We're small and busy. Keep both in mind.
known: {name}. I hear good things. And one or two of the other kind.
[m]Morning, {name}. The village is awake. So am I, unfortunately.
[d]Afternoon, {name}. Walk with me a moment.
[e]Evening, {name}. The lamps are lit. Not a bad day.
{name}. {village} has taken note of you. Bear that in mind.
friend: {name}. {village} has a word for people like you, and it isn't stranger.
[m]Morning, {name}. Sit. I'll tell you what the ledgers won't.
You've done us proud, {name}. Don't let it go to your head.
Welcome, {name}. The chair by the hearth is yours, any day.
[e]Evening, {name}. I've news to share and a stew to offer.
kin: {name}. You're one of ours. The village has decided, and so have I.
My door's open, {name}. It always was. Now it's yours as well.
[m]Morning, {name}. {village} sleeps easier with you about.
Welcome home, {name}. I'll not make a speech. The bell will.
[e]Sit with me, {name}. The village can manage without us for an hour.

stranger: Quiet, please. The ink is wet.
Books are not toys. Look, do not touch.
[m]I copy the records. If you want a book, ask politely.
Hunters rarely read. Prove me wrong.
Keep clear of the candle. Paper burns, and so do tempers.
known: {name}. Your name's in the ledger. Spelt correctly, I hope.
[m]Morning, {name}. Fresh ink, fresh pages.
[d]Afternoon, {name}. Looking for a book, or a quiet seat?
[e]Evening, {name}. I stay late. The light is kinder.
Good to see you, {name}. Mind the spine on that one.
friend: {name}! I saved you a passage. A good one.
[m]Morning, {name}. I wrote a line about you. Don't read it yet.
Sit, {name}. You may touch the books. Gently.
A hunter who listens. Rare. Sit down, {name}.
[e]Come, {name}. The best page is the one nobody's turned.
kin: {name}. You're in the margins of every page I love.
My desk, my lamp, my ink, {name}. All yours, as ever.
[m]Morning, {name}. I copied out your deeds in my best hand.
Our {name}. {village} writes you into its history. I hold the pen.
[n]Writing late, {name}? So am I. Stay awhile.

stranger: Stand wide of the anvil. Scale flies.
[m]Fire's lit, anvil's warm. State your business or leave.
Sparks fly. Don't let them find you.
A hunter's blade? Mine's cheaper than the city's.
Mind the bellows.
known: {name}. That edge has seen better days. I can hear it.
[m]Morning, {name}. Fire's up. Bring me iron.
[d]Afternoon, {name}. The hammer's tired. The metal isn't.
[e]Evening, {name}. Last piece of the day, cooling.
Good to see you, {name}. Your armour wants tightening.
friend: {name}! Let me look at that blade. You treat it like a stick.
[m]Morning, {name}. I hung a fresh edge on the spare. Don't thank me.
Pull up the stool, {name}. Watch me work. Learn something.
For you, {name}, the good coals.
[e]The forge likes you, {name}. It hasn't burned you yet.
kin: {name}. Whatever you break, I'll mend. It's the family discount.
[m]Morning, {name}. I made you something. Hush, it isn't finished.
Our {name}. The anvil rings truer when you're in the door.
Stand by the fire, {name}. Warm your hands, then tell me your troubles.
[n]The forge never sleeps for kin, {name}. What do you need?

stranger: Feet off the benches.
[e]Fire's lit inside. Coin on the counter.
Room, meal or just a seat? Pick one.
[m]Too early for ale. Tea?
Hunters drink the same as anyone. Sit.
known: {name}! Your seat's waiting.
[e]Evening, {name}. First pint's on me. Second's on you.
[m]Morning, {name}. Bread, eggs, the works. Sit.
[d]Afternoon, {name}. Quiet. Perfect for talking.
Back again, {name}. The regulars keep asking after you.
friend: {name}! Your corner by the fire is warm. Go on.
[e]Evening, {name}. I saved the good barrel. Don't tell the miners.
[m]Morning, {name}. Porridge with honey. Don't argue.
You make the place feel busy, {name}. I like that.
Sit, {name}. Supper's on me, and the story's on you.
kin: {name}. Your room's aired, your bed's turned, your mug's polished.
The inn is your house, {name}. I just hold the door.
[e]Evening, {name}. Stew's on, and there's always enough.
[m]Morning, {name}. I made too much breakfast on purpose.
[n]Late, {name}? Come in. I'll leave the fire up.

stranger: Mind the sacks. Flour travels.
[m]Wheel's turning, grain's grinding. Move along.
Mind the stones. They bite.
Wheat or barley? Either way, it's heavy.
Hunters eat bread too, I hope.
known: {name}! The wheel sings when you're near.
[m]Morning, {name}. First grind of the day.
[d]Afternoon, {name}. Water's high. Good for the wheel.
[e]Evening, {name}. The stones are quiet. So am I.
Good to see you, {name}. Flour on your boots. Mine, probably.
friend: {name}! Fresh flour, fresh bread, fresh news.
[m]Morning, {name}. Take a handful. Feel how fine.
Stay for the next grind, {name}. It's soothing.
The wheel turns better with friends about, {name}. Superstition, but still.
[e]Sit on a sack, {name}. They're clean. Mostly.
kin: {name}. Whatever flour you need, it's yours.
[m]Morning, {name}. The first loaf of the harvest is for you.
Our {name}. The mill runs on water and good company.
I'd grind the stones to dust for you, {name}. Please don't make me.
[n]Late, {name}? The wheel never rests. Come in.

stranger: Mind the linen, it's wet.
Not a drop on my linen, mind.
[m]The lines are full. Duck, or go round.
Hunters' clothes are the worst. Gate muck sticks.
Round the back, there's wet linen about.
known: [m]Morning, {name}. Good drying weather.
{name}. Your coat could do with a wash. Just saying.
[d]Afternoon, {name}. The water's cold. My hands are colder.
[e]Evening, {name}. Lines are down, folded and done.
Good to see you, {name}. Bring your laundry. Politely.
friend: {name}! Hand over that shirt. I'll have it spotless.
[m]Morning, {name}. Sheets on the line. Borrow one if you like.
Sit on the stone, {name}. Warm from the sun.
You wash more than most hunters, {name}. Or I've started noticing.
[e]{name}, I mended that tear in your cloak. I didn't ask.
kin: {name}. Whatever's dirty, bring it. Whatever's torn, I'll mend it.
[m]Morning, {name}. Clean linen on your bed. Go and lie in it.
Our {name}. The river carries your muck away. I carry the rest.
I'd wash the whole world for you, {name}. Start with your boots.
[n]Rinsing late, {name}. Help, or just keep me company.

stranger: [e]Lamps first. Talk once there's light to see by.
Step off the lane while I reach, if you would.
[m]Lamps are out, wicks cooling. Long night, that.
Don't dawdle in the dark between posts. Lamp to lamp.
[n]Trimmed and burning. You ought to be indoors.
known: [e]Evening, {name}. Yours is the first lane I do.
[m]Morning, {name}. Every lamp held through. Bar the one.
{name}! Walk lamp to lamp tonight, and the dark can't have you.
[d]Afternoon, {name}. Oil's running low. The wicks are fine.
[n]Late, {name}. Carry a lantern. I always do.
friend: {name}! I lit the lamp by your door first. Superstition.
[e]Walk the round with me, {name}. I'll show you how it's done.
[m]Morning, {name}. Dawn's your hour and mine.
Light suits you, {name}.
[n]Out late, {name}? Take a taper. Go slowly.
kin: {name}. Every lamp in {village} burns a little brighter for you.
[e]Evening, {name}. I'll light your way home. I always will.
Our {name}. The Watch sleeps easier by my lamps, and so do I.
[m]Morning, {name}. The lamps are out. You're in. Good.
[n]Take my lantern, {name}. I'll light another.

stranger: No touching the rope, please.
[m]Dawn bell's mine. Don't linger under it.
Learn the strokes and you'll always know the hour.
It's loud. It's meant to be.
[e]Dusk soon. Mind the lane.
known: {name}! I tolled it a little warmer today. You'll not have noticed.
[m]Morning, {name}. Bell's warm. Rope's cold.
[d]Afternoon, {name}. Quiet hour. My ears are grateful.
[e]Evening, {name}. Rope's ready.
{name}. The bell has learnt your step. So have I.
friend: {name}! Come, pull the rope. Gently. Don't break it.
[m]Morning, {name}. The bell sounds sweeter when you listen.
Stay for the next stroke, {name}. Feel the tower hum.
You know the bell's moods, {name}. Few do.
[e]I'll toll it soft tonight, {name}.
kin: {name}. The bell rings for {village}. And for you.
[m]Morning, {name}. First stroke is yours. Pull.
Our {name}. When you're away, the bell sounds lonelier.
{name}, home at last. The tower will want to know.
[n]Night bell, {name}. Soft, so the sleepers don't stir.

stranger: Hold there. Who are you, and why here?
[n]Nobody walks the lane at this hour without a reason. Yours?
Keep it sheathed in the village.
State your name. Or don't, and I'll remember you anyway.
[e]Dusk soon. Be indoors or be seen.
known: {name}. Quiet night so far. Keep it that way.
[n]Nothing stirring, {name}. Not tonight.
[m]Morning, {name}. We made it through the night. Good.
[d]Afternoon, {name}. Off shift, and bored already.
Walk safe, {name}. Dark comes early.
friend: {name}! The Watch remembers its debts. All of us do.
[n]Walk the round with me, {name}. Better company, same dark.
[m]Morning, {name}. We held the night. Only just.
You make the rest of us look good, {name}. We resent it.
[e]I'll stand your watch if you stand mine, {name}. Deal?
kin: {name}. You're Watch, badge or no badge.
[n]The night's yours too, {name}. We keep it together.
Our {name}. The whole Watch asks after you.
[m]Morning, {name}. We sleep easier with you out there.
If anything comes, you'll hear the bell first, {name}. Promise.

stranger: If you're bleeding, mind the floor. I've just scrubbed it.
[m]Drink water. Eat something. Then talk.
Hunters come back in pieces. Mind yourself.
Nothing in the cupboard is for show. Don't touch.
[e]Evening. Sit. Let me see that arm.
known: {name}. You're limping less. I'm pleased.
[m]Morning, {name}. Slept well? Liar.
[d]Afternoon, {name}. Cough drops are in the jar.
[e]Evening, {name}. Sit. Drink. Don't argue.
Good to see you, {name}. Mind your ribs.
friend: {name}! Let me look at you. Eat, drink, then explain the bruise.
[m]Morning, {name}. Fresh poultices. Smells awful. Works wonders.
You never drink water, {name}. Start.
I've stitched worse on a goat, {name}. Sit.
[e]Tea, {name}. Honey. No hunter nonsense.
kin: {name}. Whatever hurts, I'll mend it. Whatever hurts worse, I'll listen.
My cupboard is yours, {name}. Every herb. Every bandage.
[m]Morning, {name}. Did you sleep? Did you eat? Did you drink?
Our {name}. Don't make me sew you again. I'm out of thread.
[n]Night call, {name}? I'm awake. I always am.

stranger: Are you the one from the gates?
I'm not allowed to talk to hunters. I'm only talking a bit.
Is your sword real? Can I hold it? No? Fine.
[m]I'm not meant to be up yet.
[n]I'm not meant to be out. Don't tell.
known: It's you! I knew your boots.
{name}! Can you jump the wall? I can't. Yet.
[m]Morning, {name}! I fed a chicken!
[e]{name}, watch me run! I'm faster than a sheep!
Hello {name}! I found a frog.
friend: {name}! We're playing hunters and you're the best one!
{name}, watch me jump the stream! Watch, watch!
[m]{name}! I saved you a berry. It's squished.
[e]{name}, tell me about a gate! The scary bit!
I told everyone you're my friend, {name}. They didn't believe me.
kin: {name}! You're home! You're home!
I'm going to be a hunter like you, {name}, but with a pony.
[m]{name}! Did you bring me anything? A tooth? A claw?
[e]{name}, sit with me! I'll show you the best puddle.
[n]I can't sleep, {name}. Will you sit till I do?

stranger: Bells were louder when I was young. So was everyone.
Hm. Another hunter. The last one left muddy boots and a gate.
[m]Up early. Old habit. Old knees, too.
[e]Evening. Strangers used to bring news. Now they bring swords.
You'll want the inn. It's that way. Don't ask me twice.
known: Ah, {name}. The hunter.
[m]Morning, {name}. Sun's on my knees. Lovely.
[d]Afternoon, {name}. I was only resting my eyes.
[e]Evening, {name}. Slow down. You'll see more.
{name}. I remember when this lane was a mud track. It still is.
friend: {name}! Come here and let me look at you.
[m]Morning, {name}. My grandson won't stop talking of you.
Sit, {name}. I've a story. It's long, and half of it's true.
You've a kind face, {name}. For a hunter.
[e]The bench is warm, {name}. Sit. Tell me about the gates.
kin: {name}. You're family to me, and I'm too old to lie.
[m]Morning, {name}. Wrap up, it's cold.
Our {name}. Come, sit, eat. You're all bones.
I told the neighbours you're ours, {name}. They agreed.
[n]Can't sleep, {name}? Nor can I. Sit with me.

stranger: [m]Morning. If you've come for ore, you've come to the right door.
Looking to buy? Iron's fresh up from the second level.
Mind the carts on the way in. They don't stop for anyone.
known: {name}. Back for more of the mine's iron?
[e]Evening, {name}. The night's haul is just in.
There's a lode map on the shelf if you're of a mind to go looking.
friend: {name}! The miners asked after you this morning.
For you, friend, the good ore. Not the slag the strangers get.
kin: {name}, you're family here. Take what you need.
Kin of the mine, are you? Then you'll know where the good seams run.

produce: Apples off the bough this morning!
Honey from the hives up the lane!
Turnips! Don't laugh, they're good turnips!
[d]Plums! Sweet as you like, while they last!
[e]Last of the day, nearly a gift!

farmer: [d]Hot enough to bake the barley standing.
shepherd: Away, away! Not that way, you daft thing.
That's the lot. Count them again.
[n]Easy now, there's no wolf here. Probably.
fisher: Fish don't care about gates. Nice change.
hunter: [e]Stand clear, coming through with a buck!
Dusk's near, and so's the pot.
[e]Wind was right for once. Got a good one.
Mind the blood on the lane. Sorry.
carter: [d]The road to Carillon's long. The cart's longer.
elder: Mind the green, the geese have opinions.
A village is a great many small jobs, done.
Someone fetch the bell-ringer, I've a notice to give.
child: I'm the king of the hill!
smith: [d]Hot as the hearth of the world in here.
Hiss! Into the water with you.
miller: More wheat, more flour, more dust.
Don't breathe in the dust. I do. Look at me.
The stones sound a bit flat today.
watch_night: [n]{hour} o'clock, and the sky is quiet!
[n]{hour} of the night! Keep your fires banked!
[n]{hour} o'clock! The Watch is awake. You needn't be!
[n]Hark! {hour} o'clock, nothing stirring on the road!
tavernkeeper: Rooms aired, beds turned, come in!
Mind the step, mind the dog!
assayer: Raw iron! Copper! Up from the deep this morning!
Lode maps! Find your own seam, read it with lapis!
Coal by the sack, ingots by the bar!

village: The mill wheel's squealed since Tuesday. The miller is sulking over it.
Somebody's goat got into the herb beds again. Nobody will own to it.
The inn's new barrel is the best in years. Or it's the new cellar.
Harvest looks fair. Not good, mind. Fair.
The well-rope frayed in the night. Replaced before breakfast.
{elder} says the green wants mowing. The sheep volunteered.
A new lamp stands by the lane. Cost three emeralds, they say.
The geese have taken against the carter. He is not pleased.
A child was caught on the mill roof again. No harm, much shouting.
The bell's gone flat since the frost. We pretend not to notice.
They're mending the dock before the rains. About time.
Fish were thin this week. The river is sulking.
Wool prices are up. Everyone's smug, the shepherds worst of all.
The smith's apprentice burned the supper and the bellows both.
[m]The cockerel's been wrong about dawn all week. We've stopped trusting it.
[d]Shearing starts Thursday. Keep a sleeve free of wool, if you can.
[e]The bell rang late tonight. The ringer swears the rope was wet.
[n]Someone left the pen gate open. We're counting sheep in the dark.
region: Folk in {region} say the roads are drier east of the ford.
Carters tell of a bridge washed out somewhere in {region}.
Early frost on the high ground in {region}. A cold winter, they say.
A caravan from Carillon crossed {region} last week. Salt, nails, news.
The harvest in {region} is mixed. Wet in the west, dry in the east.
Wolves have come down in {region}. The hunters are earning their keep.
Hunters pass along the road through {region}. Fewer than last year.
There's talk of a tax on salt in {region}. There is always talk.
The old road across {region} wants mending. Nobody wants to pay.
They say the next village over has a new bell. Ours is jealous.
[m]A drover on the road says the ford is up after the night's rain.
[e]A Carillon caravan camps a day down the road, so the carter says.
gate: A rift opened {gate} of here last night. The sky went strange.
The Watch says a gate stands {gate} of us. Nobody goes near.
Cattle won't graze {gate} of the village. Make of that what you will.
There's light {gate} of the hill again. Pale, like a bruise.
A hunter went {gate} three days ago. Haven't seen them back.
We heard it {gate} before dawn. Low, like a bell underwater.
Keep off the {gate} road. The Watch has put a rope across.
The sheep came down off the {gate} hill by themselves. Never a good sign.
[n]Look {gate} tonight. Faint, but the sky is the wrong colour.
[e]The Watch lit a second fire facing {gate}. Nobody asked why.
[m]A hunter's gone {gate} at first light. We'll hear by evening.
landmark: Something hums at {landmark} before a storm. I feel it in my teeth.
Children dare each other to touch {landmark}. Nobody has. Yet.
A pedlar camped near {landmark} and swears he heard singing.
Mist sits on {landmark} even in high summer. Don't ask.
{landmark} is worth the walk, if you've a day and good boots.
They say old coin lies buried at {landmark}. Everyone says that.
The Watch sets a lamp at {landmark} each night. Costs oil, saves sleep.
Smoke over {landmark} yesterday. Charcoal burners, we hope.
[m]Dew lies strangely at {landmark}. Always has. Nobody minds.
[e]Folk go to {landmark} to think. Or to dodge their chores.
[n]Lights at {landmark} again. Fireflies, say the optimists.

stranger: Prices are on the board. I don't haggle with strangers.
[m]Early, but here's what I've got.
Emeralds up front, goods after. House rule.
Look, don't paw. Then pay.
Take your time. Don't take my stock.
known: Good to see you, {name}. Here's what I've got.
[m]Morning, {name}. Fresh in. Fair prices.
For you, {name}, the fair price. Not the stranger's.
[e]Last stock of the day, {name}. Have a look.
friend: {name}! Friend's price. Don't spread it about.
Take a look, {name}. I've knocked a few emeralds off.
[m]Morning, {name}. The best of the lot is behind the counter. Yours.
Anything you fancy, {name}. I put the good stuff in front.
kin: {name}. Family rate. Take what you need.
For kin, the best price in {village}. And that's no boast.
Whatever you fancy, {name}. The lowest price I've got.
[m]Morning, {name}. I set aside what you like. At cost.

done: Done. Pleasure doing business.
There you go. Use it well.
Emeralds counted, goods handed. Fair's fair.
Good. Look after it.
[m]First sale of the day. Lucky omen.
[e]Last of the day, sold. I'll sleep sound.
Thank you. Tell your friends, if you've any.
Done and dusted. Mind how you carry it.
Sold. Come back when you need more.
Fair price, fair goods, fair weather. Can't ask for more.
short: Short, by the look of it. Come back when you're not.
I can't give it away. The family would starve.
A few more emeralds and it's yours.
Emeralds are the coin here, friend. Not promises.
There's work on the board. It pays in emeralds.
I'd like to. The ledger wouldn't.

board: The board's got fresh notices. Read before you rush.
Anything needing doing goes on the board. Emeralds for the doing.
Folk pin up what they can't do themselves. Have a look.
[m]Board's been filling since dawn. Someone's busy.
[e]Last notices of the day. Take one for the morning.
Pinned up by the bell. Honest work, honest pay.
Everything this village needs is pinned there, in bad handwriting.
{elder} reads every notice. Nothing goes up unchecked.
done: That's it done? Bless you. Here are your emeralds.
You've saved us a day's work. Emeralds, as promised.
Fair work, fairly paid. {village} won't forget it.
I'd say thank you twice, but the emeralds say it better.
[m]Done before noon, too. I should have offered more.
[e]Just in time for supper. Come, and take your coin.
Word will go round, {name}. Good word, for once.
You have my thanks and my emeralds, in that order.
A promise kept. Not many keep them. Take your pay.
People will remember this. I will.
none: Nothing posted today. The village is, for once, coping.
Board's bare. Enjoy it, it never lasts.
No notices. Nothing broke, nobody lost anything. Marvellous.
[m]Nothing yet. Check back at noon, folk think better after breakfast.
[e]Nothing today. Come back tomorrow, there's always something.
Empty board. Even the geese are behaving.

offer: [e]Rooms are free, if you're staying the night.
A bed, a meal, a fire. Fancy any of them?
[n]Still awake? There's a bed upstairs with your name on it.
Tired? Stay the night. The gates will keep till morning.
[e]Dark soon. The road is no place to sleep. Stay.
[m]Not heading off yet? Another night won't hurt.
You look like you've walked far. A bed would suit you.
[n]No sense wandering at this hour. Take a room.
[d]Bed's aired and the sheets are clean. Stay if you like.
room: Top of the stairs, second door. If you fall out there, you wake in this bed.
Here's your key. Fall somewhere nasty and you'll wake here. House rule.
Room's yours. Come to grief out there and you'll find this pillow again.
Key's on the hook when you're out. Nobody takes it. Nobody dares.
Sleep sound. The Watch walks the lane.
Mind the third stair, it's loud. The bed is soft, though.
Room's warm, blankets mended. Don't snore.
If the worst happens, this is the bed you come back to.
rumour: They say a gate stands {gate} of here. The cattle won't graze that way.
A drover swore he saw the sky split {gate} last night.
{landmark} was glowing at dusk. Or it was the sunset. Depends who's drinking.
Someone's leaving cakes at {landmark}. Nobody admits it.
Carters from {region} say the roads are wet. Wet and watched.
The Watch doubled the night rounds. They won't say why. Everyone knows.
{elder} was up before dawn, pacing the green. Something's on their mind.
A hunter came through last week and paid in teeth. Monster teeth. We kept them.
The miller's lad is courting the washer's girl. Everyone knows but the pair.
A pedlar from {region} swears the moon turned green over the {gate} hills.
Two hens are laying double yolks. Nobody trusts it.
They say the Association is hiring in Carillon. Good pay. Poor odds.
My cousin in the city says the walls hum at night. Gates are close, he says.
The smith swears his anvil rang by itself on Thursday. He'd been drinking.
{region} is quiet. Too quiet, say the old men. They always say that.
A rift hung over {landmark} for an hour last week. Gone by dawn.
[n]Keep your voice down. The walls listen after dark.
[e]Heard it from the miller, who heard it from the fisher, who was drunk.
morning: [m]Morning. Sleep well? The beds are honest.
[m]Up already? Breakfast is porridge, eggs and bad jokes.
[m]Good morning. You're alive, so the bed worked.
[m]Morning. Tea's on, bread's warm. Take a seat.
[m]There you are. I'd started to think the bed had eaten you.
[m]Morning. Fire's lit, kettle's singing. Rise and shine, or just rise.
Up so soon? Sit, eat. The day can wait a bite.
[d]Slept in? Good. The roads will keep.
full: Full, I'm afraid. Every bed, and two cots in the stable.
No rooms. The harvest hands have taken the lot.
Sorry, friend. Not a pillow free. Try the barn?
[e]Full up tonight. A trader's cart rolled in. Come back tomorrow.

open: Enchanted books, bound and sealed. Choose carefully.
Each book holds a spell. Each spell, a price. Take your time.
Ink and magic in equal measure. Browse, then pay.
These came from Carillon. Don't ask how I got them.
[m]Fresh bound, still smelling of glue and sorcery.
Read the cover, not the contents. The contents bite.
[e]Candle's lit. Come and look at the shelf.
Careful with the spines. They're older than me.

news: {village} is in fair heart. The harvest will carry us if the weather holds.
The Watch asked for more oil for the night lamps. I've said yes.
{region} is restless. Carters bring news of gates, none of it good.
We've a bell, a mill and a good well. A village needs little more.
Carillon sends word by cart, now and then. The walls hold, they say.
The young ones talk of leaving for the city. I don't blame them. I'd miss them.
A gate stands {gate}. The Watch keeps eyes on it. We keep our heads down.
Whatever the gates do, {village} will plant in spring and reap in autumn.
We pay what we can in emeralds, and in bread when we can't.
{landmark} is ours to mind. Walk there, but leave nothing broken.
Hunters like you are a comfort. And a worry. Mostly the first.
Mind the Watch. They're tired, and tired folk jump at shadows.
[m]Another morning, another ledger. The village has, at least, woken.
[e]Dusk is the village's hour. Everyone home, everyone counted.
[n]A village at night is a held breath. We hold it together.

dawn: [m]Dawn bell! Time to be up, whether you like it or not.
[m]There's the bell. The fields are waiting.
[m]First light. The Watch hands over to the day.
[m]Bell's rung. Night's behind us, thank goodness.
dusk: [e]There it goes. Everyone in before dark.
[e]Bell's rung. The Watch takes the lane.
[e]Day's done. Time for supper and shutters.
Gate or no gate, we ring it all the same.

hit: Ow! I only said good morning!
Hey! I've done nothing to you!
Hunters, honestly. What's wrong with you?
That hurt! Is this how you thank people?
I'll tell {elder} about this, see if I don't.
broke: You broke that! That's someone's wall!
Hey! That's not yours to knock down!
That's a house, hunter, not a gate! Leave it be!
Who's going to fix that? You?
[n]Breaking houses in the dark? Shame on you.
I saw that. {elder} will hear of it.
Mind what you smash, friend. It's our home.
stole: Thief! I saw you at that chest!
Put it back. Now. Before the Watch hears.
[n]Creeping about at night, taking what's not yours!
I saw what you took. Put it back, or I'll shout.
trampled: Mind the crop! That's somebody's bread!
You're standing on the barley, hunter! Get off!
Careful! It took all spring to grow that.
Stick to the path! The field's not a road.
Someone's wheat, trampled flat. Bless me.
[n]Walking through fields in the dark. Look at the state of it.

night: They took {person}! Something came out of the dark and took {person}!
{person}! Somebody, please, it went {dir}, it went {dir}!
I heard {person} scream. I heard it and I couldn't move.
Ring it again! Ring it till the whole valley wakes!
It dragged {person} off toward {place}. I saw the eyes.
watch: Lanterns up! Nobody goes past the last fence alone.
It came from {dir}. Keep your eyes on the dark.
Steady. Whatever it is, it's gone for now.
Torches at the edge! Don't let it come back for another.
We can't follow it in the dark. Not without a hunter.
Hold the green. Mothers, get the little ones inside.
call: You. You've a blade. Will you help us?
{person}'s gone. Taken in the night. Please, I'll give anything.
Hunter, please, a moment. My child.
Nobody here can go where it went. You can.
ask: It took {person} in the night. Dragged off {dir}, toward {place}. You'll see the marks. Please.
My {person}. Something came out of the dark and took {person} toward {place}. The trail's plain enough. I'm begging you.
{beast} took {person}. The Watch won't go near {place}. Will you?
They say {beast} keeps what it takes, for a while. For a while. Please, go now.
again: The marks run {dir} from the last fence. Please hurry.
Follow the trail to {place}. Bring {person} home.
I can't sit still. Every hour {person}'s out there.
You said you'd go. Please. {place}, {dir}.
thanks: Thank you. Thank you. Bring {person} home to me.
Go. We'll keep a lamp lit at the door.
I'll be here. Right here by the well. Bring {person} back.
waiting_home: You found {person}? Where is... oh. Oh, bring {person} here!
reunion: You're home. You're home. Let me look at you.
Thank you. I'll never... thank you, {name}.

runner: Hunter! Wait! It's {person}, from {village}. Something took {person} in the night!
{name}! Thank goodness. {person}'s been taken, the trail runs {dir}. Come to the well!
Hold up! You're needed in {village}. {person} was taken.

bound: Get me out of this. Please get me out.
It comes back at dusk. Please hurry.
I can't feel my hands. Please.
freed: You came! You actually came. Take me home. Please.
Can't stand, my legs... hold on. I'll hold on.
I knew someone would come. I didn't. But I hoped.
carried: I've got you. I mean, you've got me.
walk: I can walk. Go on, I'm right behind you.
My legs are back. Lead on, I'll keep up.
I'll follow. Don't go too fast.
wait: I'll wait here. Come back for me?
Don't leave me out here long.
Is it far? Will you carry me?
cant_climb: I can't climb that! Hang a rope for me?
Too high for me. Is there another way? A rope?
I'll never get up there. Can you put a line down?

call: Hunter! A word, if you've one to spare.
You. You've seen the smoke over the ridge?
We've trouble coming. Will you hear it?
ask: Scouts saw the {beast} stirring. They come tomorrow night, and they bring fire. Will you stand with us?
The riftborn camp's grown fat on the ridge. Tomorrow night it comes for {village}. We'll fight, but we're farmers.
They'll come at dark tomorrow with fire arrows. If you're here, we might keep our roofs.
again: Tomorrow night. Be on the green at dusk.
The Watch is sharpening everything we own. Come at dusk.
Buckets by every door. We'll need every hand.
thanks: Then we'll hold. With you here, we'll hold.
Dusk tomorrow. We'll fill every bucket in {village}.
Good. I'll tell the Watch. They'll sleep easier. Well. Easier.
fight: They're at the fence! Here they come!
Don't let them reach the houses!
survivor: We lost everything but the clothes on us.
At least nobody's hurt. That's what matters. That's what I keep saying.
The masons say it can be built again. Can it?
Cold by the well at night. We'll manage.
Thirty years in that house. Thirty years.

search: {upper}! Shout if you can hear us!
Keep the lanterns high. Look for anything.
Spread out! Not too far, mind the drop!
ask: {person} went out before the storm and never came back. The search party's out {dir}, but it's dark. Please.
{person} should've been home hours ago. The storm came in so fast. Will you look?
We've searched till the lanterns gave out. {person}'s out there somewhere {dir}. Please.
again: Look {dir}. That's where {person} was working.
Anything at all. A scrap of cloth. Something dropped.
The ground's steep out that way. Mind the edges.
thanks: Thank you. Bring {person} home.
Take a lantern. Please find {person}.
Go. We'll keep calling.
found_call: I fell. I can't climb out. Please!
found: Oh thank the stars. My ankle's gone. Can you carry me?
You found me! I thought nobody would.
I slipped in the storm. Took me all night to stop shaking.
walk: I'll limp along behind you. Go on.
reunion: {person}! Where have you been? Oh, come here!
We searched all night. You're home. You're home.

call: Hunter. A moment, if you've one.
We've houses to raise and no timber to raise them with.
Could you spare a little time for {village}?
ask: We'll rebuild. We always do. But we need timber, stone and iron, more than we have. The counts are on the board.
The masons are ready. What they lack is wood and stone, and iron for the nails. Will you help us gather it?
Bring what you can to the notice board. Every log is a beam over somebody's bed.
again: The board says what's still wanted.
Every bit helps. The masons are itching to start.
Timber, stone and iron. The notice board has the counts.
thanks: Bless you. The masons will be glad.
We'll have roofs over everyone before the frost.
Thank you. {village} won't forget it.
working: Listen to them hammer. Best sound in the world.
Three days, the masons say. Three days and it'll be as it was.
Your beams are going up. Come and look.

dusk: Dusk, and no bell. It doesn't feel like evening.
I keep reaching for the rope.
Without the bell the night comes too quiet.
ask_stolen: They took the bell. Raiders from the camp, in the night, rope and all. A bell's bronze, and bronze is worth something to them.
Our bell's gone. Taken. You can't think how quiet the dusk is now.
The riftborn took our bell. Take it back, or the smith says he can cast a new one, given the bronze.
ask_cracked: When the gate broke, the bell cracked clean through. It came down in pieces.
Our bell split the night the gate broke. The smith could cast another, if he had the bell bronze.
The bell's cracked. A bell that won't ring is just a weight.
again: Five ingots of bell bronze. Copper and amethyst, the smith says.
Bring the bell back and hang it. The ringer's waiting.
The tower's empty. It looks wrong from every field.
thanks: Thank you. The night hunters have grown bold since it went quiet.
A village without a bell is a village asleep. Thank you.
Bless you. I'll tell the ringer.
casting: Bell bronze. Good. Give me a little while at the forge.
Now that's a fine colour. Stand back, this gets hot.
I've not cast a bell since I was an apprentice. Let's see.
cast: There she is. Heavy, mind. You'll feel her on the stairs.
Take her up the tower yourself. You've earned the first ring.
Careful with her. She'll ring true, I promise you.

ask: There's a gate {dir} of the fields. It breaks {when}, and when it does it'll spill right onto our crops. Can you close it?
That gate. It's going to break {when}. Last time one broke near us, nothing grew for a season. Please, close it.
The gate {dir}. You hunters close them, don't you? It breaks {when}.
again: Close it before it breaks. That's all I ask.
Every hour it stands, my stomach turns.
The fields are ready for harvest. Don't let it come to that.
thanks: Thank you. I'll sleep tonight.
Then go with our thanks. The fields will thank you too.
Bless you, hunter.

band: Take a turn round the fire! It's a festival!
We know three tunes. This is the best of them.
Clap along, it helps the fiddler.
Dance! Nobody's watching. Everybody's watching. Dance!
judge_good: Now that is something. That's a contender.
Oh my. I'll remember that one.
Best I've had all night. Don't tell the others.
judge_ok: That'll do. You might do better yet.
Not bad. The miller's wife brought a fine one, mind.

greet: {name}! You came back. Come in, sit, have something.
There's my hunter. I tell everyone about you, you know.
{name}! I still dream about that place. Then I dream about you coming through.
Look who it is. The one who carried me home.
{name}. Every time I see you I remember how cold it was. Thank you, again.

mouth: Can you hear anything? Anything at all?
They were on the second level. Right at the face.
Somebody bring more rope. And a lamp.
Nobody goes down alone. Not now.
I heard them knocking. I swear I heard knocking.
ask: They broke through into something on the second level. A nest. {person}'s down there with the others. Please, you can climb, you can fight. Go down for them.
The bell's for the mine. {person} and two more are trapped on the second level, past the winze. Something's down there with them. Will you go?
The face gave and there were Hollows behind it. Our people are cut off at the bottom. The ladder goes all the way down. Please.
again: Down the shaft, along the first level to the winze, then down again. They were working the face at the end.
Please hurry. The lamps down there won't last forever.
The ladder's on the town side of the shaft. Mind the winze, it's a long drop.
thanks: Thank you. Bring them up. Bring them all up.
We'll keep the rope and the lamps ready up here.
Go. I'll be right here at the mouth.
found: You came! Stay close, we'll follow you out.
Is it gone? Then get us out of here. We're right behind you.
My leg's hurt, but I can walk. Lead the way.
Lantern's out. I'll follow your light.
guarded: Not yet! They're still out there in the dark!
Get rid of them first, or we'll never make the winze.
up: Air. Real air. Oh, thank you.
I thought I'd never see the sky again.
Where's my family? Are they here?
